name: Astoria
blurb: Oldest US settlement west of the Rockies, at the Columbia's mouth; Lewis and Clark wintered nearby.

name: Banff
blurb: Canada's highest town, founded around hot springs; the Bow River and Cascade Mountain frame its main street.

name: Bellingham
blurb: College town on Bellingham Bay, gateway to Mt Baker via SR-542 and to the sandstone boulders of Larrabee and Chuckanut.

name: Bend
blurb: High-desert hub on the Deschutes River, and home to the world's very last Blockbuster video store.

name: Calgary
blurb: Where the Bow meets the Elbow; on a clear day the Rockies' front ranges line the western skyline 80 km away.

name: Columbia River
blurb: Enters WA from BC near Northport, sweeps the Big Bend past Grand Coulee and Vantage, then carves the Gorge on the Oregon line.

name: Crater Lake
blurb: Collapsed caldera of Mount Mazama, about 7,700 years old; at 594 m it's the deepest lake in the US.

name: Deception Pass
blurb: Narrow tidal channel between Whidbey and Fidalgo islands, spanned by a 1935 bridge 180 ft above ripping currents.

name: Edmonton
blurb: Alberta's capital straddles the North Saskatchewan River valley, home to North America's largest urban parkland.

name: Eugene
blurb: Track Town USA on the Willamette; the McKenzie River corridor to the Three Sisters starts just east.

name: Fraser River
blurb: BC's longest river rises near Mt Robson, loops north to Prince George, then carves the Fraser Canyon to the sea.

name: Fremont Troll
blurb: An 18-ft concrete troll under the Aurora Bridge, clutching a real VW Beetle; built in 1990 by local artists.

name: Grand Coulee Dam
blurb: The largest power producer in the US, holding back Lake Roosevelt at the head of the Grand Coulee.

name: Grouse Mountain
blurb: Home of the Grouse Grind, a 2.9 km stair-master of a trail gaining about 850 m.

name: Hurricane Ridge
blurb: A mile-high road-accessible perch in the Olympics with a tiny rope-tow ski area and in-your-face views of Mt Olympus.

name: Husky Stadium
blurb: UW's lakeside stadium on Union Bay; some fans still arrive by boat, "sailgating" before kickoff.

name: Jasper
blurb: Railway town in the Athabasca valley, badly hit by the 2024 wildfire; hub for the Skyline, Tonquin and Edith Cavell.

name: Kamloops
blurb: Sagebrush and hoodoo country where the North and South Thompson rivers meet.

name: Kelowna
blurb: Okanagan wine-and-beach city on the shore of Okanagan Lake, supposed home of the lake monster Ogopogo.

name: Lake Chelan
blurb: A 50-mile glacial trench over 1,480 ft deep, with its bottom below sea level; the only road-free way to Stehekin is by boat or on foot.

name: Lake Louise
blurb: Glacial flour from the Victoria Glacier turns it that milky turquoise; the hamlet sits about 4 km downhill.

name: Leavenworth
blurb: Faux-Bavarian village at the mouth of Icicle Canyon, basecamp for the Enchantments, Snow Creek Wall and endless granite boulders.

name: Microsoft Campus (Redmond)
blurb: Sprawling Redmond HQ along SR-520; plenty of engineers here sneak out to Snoqualmie Pass for night skiing.

name: Mount Hood
blurb: Oregon's highest peak at 3,429 m; the south side route via the Hogsback is one of the most-climbed glaciated peaks.

name: Mt Adams
blurb: Washington's second-highest; the South Spur is a walk-up and a famous glissade chute, with Lunch Counter camp around 9,000 ft.

name: Mt Baker
blurb: Holds the world record for single-season snowfall, 1,140 inches in 1998-99, and the Easton and Coleman glaciers are classic first volcano climbs.

name: Mt Rainier
blurb: At 14,410 ft the most glaciated peak in the Lower 48; Disappointment Cleaver is the trade route most summiteers slog.

name: Mt Robson
blurb: At 3,954 m it's the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies, and its summit is famously shrouded in cloud most days.

name: Mt St Helens
blurb: Lost 1,300 ft of summit in 1980; the Monitor Ridge permit climb ends at a crater rim looking straight into the lava dome.

name: Multnomah Falls
blurb: Two-tier falls dropping about 189 m, with the Benson Bridge spanning between the tiers.

name: Nanaimo
blurb: Harbour city on Vancouver Island's east coast, and namesake of the famous no-bake bar.

name: Okanagan Lake
blurb: A 135 km long glacial trench lake stretching from Vernon to Penticton.

name: Penticton
blurb: Squeezed between Okanagan and Skaha lakes, with world-class gneiss cragging just south of town.

name: Pike Place Market
blurb: Running since 1907, home of the flying fish and the gum wall; the original Starbucks sits across the street.

name: Portland
blurb: City of bridges at the Willamette-Columbia confluence, with Mt Hood on the eastern skyline.

name: Prince George
blurb: Northern BC's hub at the confluence of the Fraser and Nechako rivers.

name: Salem
blurb: Oregon's capital, midway up the Willamette Valley; Silver Falls and its Trail of Ten Falls lie just east.

name: San Juan Island
blurb: Home of Friday Harbor and Lime Kiln Point, one of the best shore spots in the world to watch orcas pass by.

name: Snoqualmie Falls
blurb: A 268-ft plunge on the Snoqualmie River, taller than Niagara, and famous from the opening credits of Twin Peaks.

name: Space Needle
blurb: Built for the 1962 World's Fair; its 605 ft top is a pale shadow of the Rainier you can see from it on a clear day.

name: Spokane
blurb: Eastern WA's biggest city, built around the falls of the Spokane River; Mt Spokane ski area sits just to the northeast.

name: Stanley Park
blurb: A 400-hectare forested peninsula ringed by the Seawall, bigger than Central Park in NYC.

name: Vancouver
blurb: Ski, climb and kayak on the same spring day: the North Shore peaks rise straight out of the city's backyard.

name: Victoria
blurb: BC's capital sits at the southern tip of Vancouver Island, gazing across the strait at the Olympics.

name: Whidbey Island
blurb: Long, skinny island stretching from Deception Pass to the Clinton ferry; one of the longest islands in the Lower 48.

name: Whistler
blurb: Host of the 2010 Olympic alpine events and jumping-off point for the Spearhead and Fitzsimmons traverses.

name: Whitehorse
blurb: Yukon's capital on the Yukon River, once the head of sternwheeler navigation for Klondike stampeders.

name: Athabasca Glacier
blurb: Toe of the Columbia Icefield, visible from the Parkway; it has retreated well over a kilometre since the 1840s.

name: Bugaboos
blurb: Granite spires jutting from Purcell glaciers; Conrad Kain climbed Bugaboo Spire in 1916 and called it his hardest ascent.

name: Canmore
blurb: Former coal-mining town turned climbing and ski-touring base, tucked under the Three Sisters and Ha Ling.

name: Cannon Beach
blurb: Named after a cannon washed ashore from USS Shark in 1846; Haystack Rock towers off the beach.

name: Cape Flattery
blurb: Most northwesterly point of the contiguous US, on the Makah Reservation; sea caves and Tatoosh Island just offshore.

name: Colchuck Lake
blurb: Turquoise lake beneath Dragontail and Colchuck Peak; the jumping-off point for Aasgard Pass and the Enchantments thru-hike.

name: Coquihalla Hwy
blurb: Highway 5 from Hope to Kamloops, star of Highway Thru Hell; the summit near Zopkios is a classic ski tour.

name: Crystal Mountain
blurb: Washington's largest ski area, with a gondola to the summit and a face-full view of Rainier from the top.

name: Dawson City
blurb: Heart of the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush, sitting where the Klondike River joins the Yukon.

name: Diablo Lake
blurb: Glacial flour turns this reservoir an unreal turquoise; Colonial Peak and Pyramid Peak tower over the SR-20 overlook.

name: Discovery Park
blurb: Seattle's biggest park on the old Fort Lawton grounds in Magnolia, with bluffs and a lighthouse at West Point.

name: Drumheller
blurb: Badlands town in the Red Deer River valley; hoodoos, dinosaur bones and the Royal Tyrrell Museum.

name: Dry Falls
blurb: Skeleton of an ice-age waterfall 3.5 miles wide and 400 ft tall, once roaring with Missoula Flood water.

name: Enchantments
blurb: The one-day thru-hike: Colchuck, up Aasgard Pass, across the larch-lined Core Zone and down past Snow Lakes, about 18 miles.

name: Fernie
blurb: Coal-mining town turned ski mecca in the Lizard Range, famed for its deep powder storm cycles.

name: Garibaldi Lake
blurb: Its startling turquoise water is held back by The Barrier, a lava dam of unstable volcanic rock.

name: Golden
blurb: Where the Kicking Horse meets the Columbia; a base for the Rockies, Purcells and Rogers Pass.

name: Haida Gwaii
blurb: An archipelago of about 150 islands off the north coast, sometimes called the Galápagos of Canada.

name: Hoh Rainforest
blurb: One of the wettest places in the Lower 48 at 12+ ft of rain a year, and the long approach trail to Mt Olympus.

name: Icefields Parkway
blurb: Highway 93N: 232 km from Lake Louise to Jasper, topping out at Bow Summit and passing a hundred-odd glaciers.

name: Joffre Lakes
blurb: Three glacier-fed lakes stacked beneath Matier Glacier, just off the Duffey Lake Road.

name: Kluane Lake
blurb: Yukon's largest lake, beside the Alaska Highway at the edge of Kluane National Park.

name: Lake Crescent
blurb: Glacier-carved, over 600 ft deep and famously clear, tucked below Mount Storm King west of Port Angeles.

name: Moraine Lake
blurb: Sits under the Valley of the Ten Peaks; the rockpile at its outlet is probably a rockslide, not a moraine at all.

name: Mount Bachelor
blurb: Young Cascade volcano and big ski area; lifts reach the summit, so skiing 360 degrees off the top is possible.

name: Mount Jefferson
blurb: Oregon's second-highest peak, 3,199 m; its exposed summit pinnacle turns back many parties.

name: Mount Si
blurb: The North Bend training grind: 3,150 ft of gain in 4 miles, topped by the exposed Haystack scramble.

name: Mountain Loop Hwy
blurb: Granite Falls to Darrington via Barlow Pass; gravel over the top, winter-gated, and access to Vesper, Pilchuck, Big Four and Sloan.

name: Mt Baker Ski Area
blurb: Legendary snowfall, cliffy lift-served terrain and the Legendary Banked Slalom; runs up from Heather Meadows under Shuksan.

name: Mt Garibaldi
blurb: A heavily eroded stratovolcano whose rubbly Atwell Peak dominates the view north from Squamish.

name: Mt Olympus
blurb: Highest in the Olympics at 7,980 ft; a 17-mile walk in, the Blue Glacier crossing, then a short rock summit block.

name: Nelson
blurb: Heritage mountain town on Kootenay Lake's West Arm, home to Whitewater's deep powder.

name: North Bend
blurb: Last stop for coffee before Snoqualmie Pass, overshadowed by Mount Si, and the real-world Twin Peaks town.

name: North Cascades Hwy (SR-20)
blurb: Opened in 1972, crossing Rainy and Washington passes; closed each winter by avalanches, and its spring reopening is a local holiday.

name: Palouse Falls
blurb: A 198-ft drop into a basalt amphitheater carved by the Missoula Floods; the official state waterfall.

name: Pemberton
blurb: Seed-potato farming valley under Mt Currie's 1,700 m north face, at the start of the Duffey Lake Road.

name: Port Hardy
blurb: Near the north tip of Vancouver Island, where BC Ferries' Inside Passage run departs for Prince Rupert.

name: Rattlesnake Ledge
blurb: A short, relentlessly busy switchback climb from Rattlesnake Lake to a rock ledge high above the water.

name: Revelstoke
blurb: Powder town between the Selkirks and Monashees, with the most vertical of any lift-served resort in North America.

name: Sea-to-Sky Hwy
blurb: Highway 99 climbs from Howe Sound past the Chief and Brandywine Falls to Whistler and Pemberton.

name: Sisters
blurb: Western-themed village named for the Three Sisters volcanoes that crowd its skyline to the southwest.

name: Skagit River
blurb: Dammed three times above Newhalem, then free-flowing past Marblemount to the delta; winter bald eagles gather by the hundreds.

name: Smith Rock
blurb: Birthplace of American sport climbing: To Bolt or Not to Be at the Dihedrals became the first US 5.14a in 1986.

name: Snoqualmie Pass
blurb: I-90 crest at just 3,022 ft, lowest of the major Cascade passes, with four ski areas and the Alpental backcountry right off the exit.

name: Squamish
blurb: The Outdoor Recreation Capital of Canada: granite big walls, kiteboarding, mountain biking and bald eagles.

name: Stevens Pass
blurb: US-2 crest at 4,061 ft and home of Stevens Pass ski area; the PCT crosses right through the parking lots.

name: The Chief
blurb: The Stawamus Chief is a 700 m granite monolith; the Grand Wall is one of Canada's most iconic rock climbs.

name: Three Sisters
blurb: North, Middle and South Sister, all over 3,000 m; South Sister is a popular walk-up with a crater lake on top.

name: Tofino
blurb: Surf town at the end of Hwy 4 on Vancouver Island's wild west coast, gateway to Clayoquot Sound.

name: Vantage
blurb: Columnar basalt cliffs of Frenchman Coulee, a side channel scoured out by the Ice Age floods above the Columbia.

name: Washington Pass
blurb: SR-20 hairpin under Liberty Bell and the Early Winters Spires; high point of the North Cascades Hwy at 5,477 ft.

name: Waterton
blurb: Waterton Park townsite, where prairie slams into mountains; boat to Crypt Lake trailhead leaves from here.

name: Winthrop
blurb: Wild West-themed Methow town with world-class Nordic trails; first stop east when SR-20 reopens in spring.

name: Yakima
blurb: Hop capital of the US: the Yakima Valley grows roughly three quarters of the nation's hops.

name: Alvord Desert
blurb: Dry lakebed under Steens' east scarp, flat enough for land-speed records; hot springs on the edge.

name: Bella Coola
blurb: Tidewater village at the end of Hwy 20 and 'The Hill,' ringed by heli-ski terrain in the Coast Range.

name: Blue Glacier
blurb: The big glacier cloaking Mt Olympus; crossing it from Glacier Meadows is the crux of the standard climb.

name: Bongos
blurb: Caribbean cafe in a converted 76 gas station on Aurora; a sandpit now sits where the pumps used to be.

name: Brave New World
blurb: 5.14d, hardest sport route in Washington.

name: Broken Top
blurb: Heavily eroded stratovolcano exposing its layered innards; the Crater Ditch and Green Lakes approaches are classics.

name: Cape Scott
blurb: The storm-lashed northwest tip of Vancouver Island, end of the North Coast Trail.

name: Carcross Desert
blurb: Sand dunes left by an ancient glacial lake bed, often billed as one of the world's smallest deserts.

name: Cascade Pass
blurb: Meadowed notch below Johannesburg's hanging glaciers; start of Sahale Arm and the Ptarmigan Traverse.

name: Castle Mountain
blurb: Crenellated massif over the Bow Valley; Eisenhower Tower anchors its SE end, reached from a popular climbers' hut.

name: Castle Rock (Leavenworth)
blurb: Tumwater Canyon crag above US-2, climbed since the 1940s; Saber is the classic that let generations cut their teeth.

name: Chilkoot Trail
blurb: The 1898 stampeders' route over Chilkoot Pass; the Canadian half drops past Lindeman Lake to Bennett.

name: Chinook Pass Hwy (SR-410)
blurb: Enumclaw to Naches, cresting at Chinook Pass by Tipsoo Lake; winter-closed, and the gateway to Crystal and Sunrise.

name: Crypt Lake
blurb: Boat approach, ladder, and a crawl through a rock tunnel lead to this lake right against the US border.

name: Darrington
blurb: Logging town under Whitehorse Mountain, with long granite slab climbs on Squire Creek Wall and Exfoliation Dome nearby.

name: Deschutes River
blurb: Rises at Little Lava Lake, loops south through Wickiup, then runs north past Bend and Maupin to the Columbia. Big whitewater.

name: Dog Mountain
blurb: Steep Columbia Gorge grind famous for its spring balsamroot bloom and ferocious gorge winds on top.

name: Dragontail Peak
blurb: Highest in the Enchantments, with the Backbone Ridge and Serpentine Arête rising straight out of Colchuck Lake.

name: Duffey Lake Rd
blurb: Highway 99 from Mount Currie to Lillooet; Cayoosh Pass at the top has endless ski touring right off the road.

name: Eagle Cap
blurb: Centerpiece of the Wallowas' granite high country; radiating valleys give the wilderness its name.

name: Eldorado Peak
blurb: Queen of the Cascade River; a brutal boulder-field approach then a knife-edge snow arête to the summit.

name: Emmons Glacier
blurb: Largest glacier by area in the Lower 48, on Rainier's northeast flank; the Emmons-Winthrop route camps at Schurman.

name: Fall City
blurb: Riverside hamlet at the Raging River mouth on the Snoqualmie; the back road to North Bend without touching I-90.

name: Flyboys
blurb: 18-pitch 5.9 sport line up Mazama's Goat Wall, bolted in 2016-17 with crowdfunded hardware from Washington climbers.

name: Forbidden Peak
blurb: West Ridge is one of the Fifty Classic Climbs, reached via Boston Basin; exposed, heavily trafficked, rarely easy.

name: Glacier Peak
blurb: The most remote Cascade volcano, a long approach from any road and barely visible from Seattle.

name: Goat Rocks
blurb: Eroded volcano between Rainier and Adams; the PCT runs its crest along the Knife Edge past Old Snowy.

name: Gold Bar
blurb: Small US-2 town and the last gas and grub before the Index walls and Stevens Pass; Wallace Falls is just above it.

name: Golden Hinde
blurb: At 2,195 m it's Vancouver Island's highest peak, deep in the backcountry of Strathcona Park.

name: Ha Ling Peak
blurb: Named for a Chinese cook who reportedly climbed it on a bet in 1896; Canmore's favourite quick hike.

name: Historic Columbia River Highway
blurb: Opened 1916 as America's first planned scenic highway, looping past Vista House and the waterfalls to The Dalles.

name: Howser Towers
blurb: The Bugaboos' highest summit; the Beckey-Chouinard on South Howser Tower is one of the Fifty Classic Climbs.

name: I-90 Exit 32 (Mt Si/Little Si)
blurb: 436th Ave SE exit, the fast way to the Mount Si and Little Si trailheads and to Rattlesnake Lake via Cedar Falls Rd.

name: I-90 Exit 38 (Deception Crags/Olallie)
blurb: Homestead Valley Rd exit for Deception Crags sport climbing, Twin Falls and Olallie State Park along the old highway.

name: I-90 Exit 47 (Denny Creek/Asahel Curtis)
blurb: Tinkham Rd exit: Denny Creek, Melakwa Lake, Annette Lake and the Asahel Curtis trailheads just west of the pass.

name: Index
blurb: Tiny town under Mount Index and the Town Walls, where the North and South Forks of the Skykomish meet.

name: Index Town Walls
blurb: Steep granite cliffs over the Skykomish with hard cracks and old-school trad; the Lower and Upper Town Walls hover over the town.

name: Infinite Bliss
blurb: 23 bolted pitches and ~2600 ft up a south-side gully of Mt Garfield's West Peak, billed as North America's longest sport climb.

name: Lake Agnes Tea House
blurb: Built by the CPR in 1901; everything is hauled up on foot or by helicopter, and there's no electricity.

name: Lake O'Hara
blurb: A Yoho gem reachable by a limited-seat bus or a long walk; Abbot Pass hut sat above it until 2022.

name: Lake Serene
blurb: Tucked in the cirque under Mount Index's sheer north face; Bridal Veil Falls roars along the way up.

name: Liberty Bell
blurb: Iconic granite spire above Washington Pass; the Beckey Route is a short classic, and the east faces are big walls.

name: Maligne Lake
blurb: Largest natural lake in the Canadian Rockies; Spirit Island is reached by boat from the north end.

name: Marblemount
blurb: Last services before the North Cascades crest; climbers get their backcountry permits at the Wilderness Information Center here.

name: Mazama
blurb: Upper Methow outpost with a famous general store, gateway to Washington Pass climbing and Harts Pass.

name: Miles Canyon
blurb: Basalt-walled gorge on the Yukon River just upstream of Whitehorse that wrecked many stampeders' boats.

name: Mount Alberta
blurb: First climbed by a Japanese party in 1925, who reportedly left an ice axe on top; still one of the Rockies' hardest summits.

name: Mount Columbia
blurb: Highest point in Alberta at 3,747 m, perched on the Divide at the far edge of the Columbia Icefield.

name: Mount Edith Cavell
blurb: Its 1,500 m north face, first climbed in 1961, is one of North America's classic alpine climbs.

name: Mount Sir Douglas
blurb: Kananaskis's highest summit at 3,406 m, straddling the Divide, with a glaciated approach over the Haig Glacier.

name: Mount Temple
blurb: At 3,544 m the highest peak in the Lake Louise area; scrambler's route up the SW side, while the north face is a serious alpine test.

name: Mount Thielsen
blurb: The Lightning Rod of the Cascades; fulgurites coat the needle-like summit pinnacle.

name: Mt Assiniboine
blurb: The Matterhorn of the Rockies straddles the Divide; its summit lies on the BC side in Mt Assiniboine Park.

name: Mt Begbie
blurb: A glaciated 2,733 m peak that forms Revelstoke's skyline, south of town across the Columbia.

name: Mt Constance
blurb: Third-highest in the Olympics, rising abruptly above Hood Canal; loose rock and a notorious Terrible Traverse on its route.

name: Mt Daniel
blurb: Highest point in King County, draped by the Lynch Glacier and seen from Cathedral Pass on the PCT.

name: Mt Joffre
blurb: Highest peak of the Joffre Group; its north couloir is a coveted steep ski line.

name: Mt Logan
blurb: Canada's highest peak at 5,959 m, with perhaps the largest base circumference of any mountain on Earth.

name: Mt Shuksan
blurb: One of the most-photographed mountains anywhere; Fisher Chimneys and the Sulphide Glacier lead to a rocky summit pyramid.

name: Mt Sir Donald
blurb: Its Northwest Ridge offers roughly 1,000 m of quartzite scrambling, a Rogers Pass rite of passage.

name: Mt Slesse
blurb: Its knife-edged NE Buttress is a North American classic; a 1956 airliner crash site lies on its slopes.

name: Mt Stuart
blurb: One of the biggest granite masses in the US; the North Ridge is a Fifty Classic and the Cascadian Couloir is the descent everyone curses.

name: Mt Waddington
blurb: At 4,019 m the highest peak entirely in BC, a rime-plastered tower guarded by huge glaciers.

name: Painted Hills
blurb: John Day Fossil Beds unit whose red, gold and black bands record ancient soils from a warmer climate.

name: Ptarmigan Traverse
blurb: Cascade Pass to Dome Peak along the glaciated crest, first done in 1938 by four Ptarmigan Climbing Club members.

name: Rogers Pass
blurb: The railway's 1880s route through the Selkirks, now a legendary ski touring zone with a permit system.

name: Sahale Peak
blurb: Above Cascade Pass via Sahale Arm and a glacier to a tiny summit block; the Sahale Glacier camp may be the best bivy in the range.

name: Skaha Bluffs
blurb: Hundreds of sunny gneiss sport routes above Skaha Lake, a spring and fall escape from coastal rain.

name: Skeena River
blurb: BC's second-longest river flows through the Coast Mountains past Terrace to tidewater near Prince Rupert.

name: Sky Pilot
blurb: A craggy 2,031 m summit looming over the Sea to Sky Gondola, above Howe Sound.

name: Skykomish River
blurb: From the South Fork at Skykomish past Index, where the forks meet, to the Snohomish near Monroe; Boulder Drop is class IV.

name: Skyline Trail
blurb: 44 km from Maligne Lake to Maligne Canyon, with about 25 km above treeline over Big Shovel Pass and the Notch.

name: Sloan Peak
blurb: The Matterhorn of the Mountain Loop; the Corkscrew Route spirals around the peak to reach the summit.

name: Spearhead Traverse
blurb: A horseshoe ski traverse from Blackcomb to Whistler over a dozen glaciers, often done in a single long day.

name: Steamboat Rock
blurb: A basalt butte rising 800 ft out of Banks Lake in the Grand Coulee, once an island in an ice-age river channel.

name: Steens Mountain
blurb: Huge fault-block mountain; the east face drops about 1,500 m to the Alvord Desert, and a gravel road nearly reaches the top.

name: Takakkaw Falls
blurb: Fed by the Daly Glacier, it drops about 373 m in Yoho; the name comes from a Cree word for magnificent.

name: Tantalus Range
blurb: A jagged glaciated wall across the Squamish River from Hwy 99; crossings start with a river boat or a fixed rope.

name: Tatoosh Range
blurb: Craggy range just south of Paradise; Pinnacle and Unicorn peaks are fun scrambles with Rainier filling the whole sky.

name: The Brothers
blurb: Twin-summited peak visible from Seattle across the Sound; the south peak is a long but non-technical scramble from Lena Lakes.

name: The Lions
blurb: Twin granite summits above Howe Sound; the Squamish people call them the Twin Sisters.

name: Three Fingered Jack
blurb: Crumbling volcanic plug; the summit block has a famous exposed step with big air below.

name: Timberline Trail
blurb: Roughly 66 km loop around Mt Hood via Paradise Park, Ramona Falls, Cairn Basin and Cloud Cap, with unbridged glacial creek fords.

name: Tombstone Park
blurb: Jagged granite peaks along the Dempster Highway, dubbed the Patagonia of the North.

name: US-2 (Stevens Pass Hwy)
blurb: Everett to Leavenworth over Stevens Pass, past Index and Skykomish; the Tumwater Canyon stretch threads right below Castle Rock.

name: Vesper Peak
blurb: Mountain Loop classic via Headlee Pass and Vesper Lake; the north face Ragged Edge is a long, clean alpine rock route.

name: Wapta Traverse
blurb: Classic hut-to-hut ski traverse along the Divide: Peyto, Bow, Balfour and Scott Duncan huts, exiting past Sherbrooke Lake.

name: Wedge Mountain
blurb: At 2,892 m the highest summit in Garibaldi Park, reached via the Wedgemount Lake hut.

name: Yamnuska
blurb: Mount John Laurie's limestone south face, the first big wall you see driving west; a cradle of Rockies rock climbing.

name: Yukon River
blurb: The Klondike highway of 1898: paddlers still float it from Whitehorse to Dawson on a ~715 km journey.
